clue.text: Lie in certain position round top of head? It does

parts.note: pork pie is Cockney rhyming slang for a lie (pork pie = porky = lie)

indicators.note: the round top of the head is its crown, so the word head gives its first letter

parts.note: to be at a place is to be in a certain position

explanation.surface: Instructions for lying in a set position, with something round the top of the head, which turns out to be the very item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It does' is the definition: the thing that sits round the top of the head. PORK PIE is British rhyming slang for a lie; AT follows H, the top of head.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat-crowned hat is worn round the top of the head, so it is what does the job the clue describes.

clue.text: Attempt to get married in ceremony

indicators.note: the abbreviation sits in the middle of the word for an attempt

parts.note: to have a pop at something is to attempt it

explanation.surface: Someone tries to get married with a proper ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: Pomp is splendid ceremonial display, so it stands for ceremony as a close synonym.

clue.text: Remains on team keeping united

parts.note: RE means on or concerning, as in a letter heading

indicators.note: the team word holds the abbreviation inside it

parts.note: a side is a team in sport
U is the abbreviation for united, as in football club names

explanation.surface: A player stays with a team that keeps its unity.
explanation.definitionFit: Residue is what is left over, a synonym of remains as a noun.

clue.text: Frequent condition of Dad's Army — Dads protecting country admitting limits of civilians in it

indicators.note: the word for dads surrounds everything else as if guarding it

parts.note: pa is an informal word for a dad, so dads are pas

indicators.note: the country word lets the next part into itself

parts.note: a nation is a country

indicators.note: the outer letters of civilians go inside the word it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the limits of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A comment on the British wartime sitcom Dad's Army, whose Home Guard volunteers protect the country with civilians in their ranks.
explanation.walkthrough: Dad's Army is a classic British TV comedy about the WWII Home Guard, famous for Corporal Jones crying 'Don't panic!'. The containers nest three deep: 'in' innermost, then 'admitting', then 'protecting' outermost.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a state of alarm and frantic activity, which the bumbling platoon was constantly in.

clue.text: It's morally right holding indefinite number of races

indicators.note: the word for morally right holds the letter inside it

parts.note: ethical means morally right
N is used in maths for an unspecified number

explanation.surface: A claim that something is morally right while involving an uncounted number of races.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethnical is an older form of ethnic, an adjective relating to races or peoples.

clue.text: Striking fear in first section of prison?

parts.note: A is the first letter and means first, as in an A grade
a wing is a section of a prison building

explanation.surface: Asks whether the first block of a jail is where intimidation happens.
explanation.definitionFit: Awing is the participle of awe, to fill someone with fearful respect.

clue.text: Scheme cutting out middleman regularly

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of the word middleman, starting with the second

explanation.surface: A plan to cut out the middleman as a matter of routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting out' tells you letters are removed: take away M, D, L, M, N in turn and what is left is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea can be a plan or scheme for doing something.

clue.text: More than one helping what are carried out in toy hospital?

definitions.meaning: lumps or servings of food, plural helpings

definitions.text: what are carried out in toy hospital

explanation.surface: A puzzle over what a toy hospital does, mixing servings of food with surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 5,2 the answer reads as operations on dolls, the cryptic second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Dollops are large shapeless servings of food, so several helpings.

clue.text: Drama rude men might miss playing?

definitions.text: Drama rude men might miss playing?

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters being played about with into a new order

explanation.surface: The rustic mechanicals, rude men, might miss cues while playing a drama.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'rude mechanicals' are the amateur actors in this Shakespeare comedy who stage a play badly, so the whole clue describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: This Shakespeare comedy is a drama in which rough workmen put on a bungled play within the play.

clue.text: Craftsman well employed in isle

indicators.note: the word for well is used inside the island name

parts.note: the Isle of Man
so is used like well at the start of a remark

explanation.surface: A craftsman finds good work on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: A mason is a skilled worker in stone, a traditional craftsman.

clue.text: The mob's taking cut — be doubly alert about it

indicators.note: the two calls go about the word for cut

parts.note: HOI and OI are both calls to make someone alert, given twice
to poll is to cut, as with hair or horns

explanation.surface: A rabble takes a cut while someone is warned twice to stay alert.
explanation.walkthrough: The two calls differ: the second is the first without its H.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is Greek for 'the many' and is used for the common people or the masses.

clue.text: Taxation prole dodges providing that little luxury

clue.text: Is cold, got sunk, being punished with such mediaeval devices?

clue.text: Checks rubbish journalist brought back to office

tat is cheap rubbish
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A rubbish journalist is checked and then returned to the office.
explanation.definitionFit: To be restored to a former position or post is to be put back in office.

clue.text: English trade union parts open to bribery later

indicators.note: the bribable word parts to let the union in

parts.note: venal means open to bribery

explanation.surface: An English union splits open a corrupt arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventual describes what happens in the end, so later in time.

clue.text: Creature almost set problem

parts.note: to pose a question is to set it
a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: An animal nearly sets a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: The possum is an Australasian or American marsupial, an animal or creature.

clue.text: Unpleasant smell gathering all over one kind of cheese

taken as written
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A nasty smell spreading all around a type of cheese.

clue.text: See 8

clue.text: Enraged a cuckoo at 3

clue.text: Studio location of horror film with final bits cut
